_meta.rule: An entry requires BOTH a `verification` (what outside the instrument it agrees with) and a `falsification` (the measurement that would have shown it wrong, and its outcome). Inputs -- material properties, physical constants, requirements -- carry `source` instead, and are marked kind=input. Results carry kind=result. error:null means UNMEASURED, never zero.
_meta.entries: starts EMPTY by design: nothing is inherited from ../waveguide without re-derivation
_meta.indirection: A NAME ALONE MUST NOT RESOLVE. Entries with a `contexts` list hold several recorded values discriminated by context (solver, mesh, extraction, ne, ...). values.get(name, **context) returns one or REFUSES, printing the alternatives. Added 2026-08-25 after CONVENTIONS 7aq/7at: every serious error in that window was one name meaning different measured things in different contexts. Legacy single-value entries (no `contexts`) still resolve.

torch.sapphire.permittivity.material: single-crystal sapphire (Al2O3), eps PERPENDICULAR to the anisotropy (c) axis — what TE011's E_phi sees when c lies along the tube axis
torch.sapphire.permittivity.source: ✅ MEASURED. Krupka J, Huang W-T, Tung M-J, 'Complex permittivity measurements of low-loss microwave ceramics employing higher order quasi TE0np modes excited in a cylindrical dielectric sample', Meas. Sci. Technol. 16 (2005) 1014-1020, doi:10.1088/0957-0233/16/4/014. Figure 10 caption: 'Dielectric loss tangents PERPENDICULAR TO THE ANISOTROPY AXIS ... The measured permittivity was 4.43 +-0.5% for single-crystal quartz and 9.39 +-0.5% for sapphire.' refs/Complex_Permittivity_Measurements_of_Low-Loss_Micr.pdf, supplied by the user 2026-08-25. 🔑 The method is TE0np modes in a cylindrical sample — the SAME mode family as this cavity.
torch.sapphire.permittivity.note: ✅ THE AXIS CORRECTION IS REAL; ITS CONSEQUENCE IS SMALLER THAN FIRST CLAIMED. Measured on this cavity (e3-torch-01 B_sap): eps 11.6 -> 9.39 moves f0 by only +3.325 MHz, a slope of 1.50 MHz per unit eps. The R-era slope of 6.56 used to predict a cancellation is 4.4x too large and does NOT transfer. So the torch shift goes from about -13.9 MHz to about -10.5 MHz -- a 24% reduction, NOT the cancellation predicted. The torch restoration keeps its urgency.
torch.sapphire.permittivity.verification: Independent of this programme, peer-reviewed, quoted uncertainty +-0.5% on the real part. Agrees with the standard uniaxial convention (eps_perp ~9.4 ordinary, eps_par ~11.6 extraordinary) that geometry.py's comment INVERTED.
torch.sapphire.permittivity.falsification: geometry.py:1416 (from R98) asserted '11.6 is eps_PERP_c ... 9.4 is eps_PARALLEL_c'. This measurement says the reverse. R32's supporting check was CIRCULAR: 'c-longitudinal reproduces isotropic 11.6' confirms only that the simulation put 11.6 on the perpendicular axis, which was the assumption under test.

torch.sapphire.loss_tangent.note: Used by e3_closure case D -> Q_dielectric 1,911,259 and the F2 bound eta_diel <= 2.27%. The BOUND survives any plausible change here because it only needs plasma loss >= 0.

wall.conductivity.s_per_m.source: R58 adopted bare electropolished aluminium on OPTICAL grounds (no plating to degrade or flake into the optical path). The conductivity is the handbook value for 6061 at 20 C, not a measurement of our surface — a real electropolished wall will fall SHORT of it, so every Q computed from this is an UPPER bound.
wall.conductivity.s_per_m.note: Declared here because this programme's baselines start empty by design and nothing is inherited without re-derivation. The MATERIAL CHOICE is inherited from R58 and still needs its own re-derivation (optical vs Q trade); the NUMBER is a handbook input, which is why kind=input and it carries source rather than verification/falsification.

torch.quartz.permittivity.material: fused quartz (amorphous SiO2) — ISOTROPIC, so no axis question
torch.quartz.permittivity.source: geometry.py filter_eps default, inherited from R107. ⚠️ NOT independently cited here. The same paper that settles sapphire (Krupka et al., Meas. Sci. Technol. 16 (2005) 1014) measures SINGLE-CRYSTAL quartz at 4.43 +-0.5% perpendicular to the anisotropy axis — a DIFFERENT material from fused quartz, so it does NOT transfer.
torch.quartz.permittivity.note: Used for the development-build torch and the retired mode-filter annulus. 🔑 Fused quartz ~3.78 is a standard handbook value and plausible, but this programme has not cited one. Marked tentative so it cannot be quoted as measured.

cavity.d_over_l.description: Cavity diameter-to-length ratio. H1's answer, and the ONLY statement of the cavity's shape.
cavity.d_over_l.source: H1, an ANALYTIC max-min over D/L for TE011 Q (KNOWN.md § H1). At 2.45 GHz it gives a = 88.0045 mm, L = 115.4158 mm. Poles to avoid: TM012 crosses TE011 at D/L = 1.096440.
cavity.d_over_l.note: 🔴 DECLARED 2026-08-25 because this number was written THREE times, twice as itself (e0k2_anchor.py, h2_groove.py) and once as a CONTRADICTORY a/L pair: e0_solver_vs_math carried A_MM,L_MM = 103.70,88.53, i.e. D/L = 2.343 — a different cavity, and the default in GEO. Every H3 rig overrode it with design_point() so the design record is consistent, but rigs that did NOT override meshed the legacy cavity. Derive a and L; never write them.
cavity.d_over_l.verification: the sidecars of every H3 mesh record radius 88.004517 / length 115.41576, which is exactly this D/L at 2.45 GHz
cavity.d_over_l.falsification: if a design-rig sidecar ever records radius 103.70, that rig did not override GEO and is on the legacy cavity

source.f0.ghz.note: Distinct from cavity.f0.cold.ghz, which is a MEASURED resonance. This is the target the geometry is solved to.

cavity.groove.mm.source: H2, validated COLD against the LDMOS tuning range. TM111 -64 MHz, TE011 Q -0.3%.
cavity.groove.mm.note: 🔴 BASELINE, NOT IMMUTABLE — loading moves every mode and refining it under load is H3's job. 🔴 DECLARED 2026-08-25 because this pair was written as a literal in SEVEN files. The groove omission (GEO never passed --groove) put 31 rigs on a cavity nobody is building; a frozen value living in seven places is the same failure waiting to happen (CONVENTIONS 7f).

loop.size.mm.note: ⚠️ FOUND ON THE CAP AT N=1. NEXT.md item 7 records that it does not transfer to another mount, and re-sweeping area is step 3 — after mount and capacitor.

loop.wire_r.mm.source: geometry.py default, inherited. ⚠️ NO PROVENANCE — one of the loop axes NEXT.md item 7 flags as never chosen.

loop.gap.mm.description: Port gap at the loop crossbar — the lumped-port face sits here.

cavity.atmosphere.description: The gas filling the cavity volume OUTSIDE the torch. Not the plasma gas.
cavity.atmosphere.source: STATED by the user 2026-08-25: 'We should check the simplest route first: just air.' A DECISION, taken deliberately as the simplest buildable option — not an inheritance.
cavity.atmosphere.note: 🔑 DECIDES THE ARCING LIMIT. Paschen breakdown over a sub-millimetre gap differs by orders of magnitude between atmospheric air, a purge, and vacuum (which would substitute multipactor instead). Before this was stated, NEXT.md 7d recorded the arcing check as UNDEFINED rather than merely unmeasured. ⚠️ Distinct from the PLASMA gas (N2) and from torch flows.

cavity.pressure.kpa.description: Cavity fill pressure — ambient, implied by an air-filled cavity open to atmosphere.
cavity.pressure.kpa.source: Follows from cavity.atmosphere = air with no sealing stated. ⚠️ DERIVED FROM AN ABSENCE: if the cavity is ever sealed or pressurised this must be re-stated, and the arcing limit moves with it.

loop.conductivity.s_per_m.source: STATED by the user 2026-08-27: 'I think the loop material being copper makes sense.' A DECISION. ⚠️ Distinct from the WALLS, which are bare electropolished aluminium 6061 at 3.5e7 (R58, optical grounds) — the two are different metals and must not be conflated.
loop.conductivity.s_per_m.note: 🔴 DECLARED BECAUSE I ASSERTED IT WITHOUT PROVENANCE. 'a copper gap' reached THREE landed documents while NEXT.md 7d.A simultaneously listed the loop material as UNSTATED — the same session both flagged the gap and filled it with an invention. The store's guard could not catch it: values.get() refuses an undeclared name, but PROSE does not go through values.get(). Now it is declared, so the claim is backed.

loop.azim.h.mm.description: AZIMUTHAL loop: height of the arc above the barrel wall, i.e. the arc sits at r = a - h. Also sets the conductor-to-wall clearance (h - half the conductor's radial thickness), which is both a capacitance and the arc risk.
loop.azim.h.mm.source: STATED by the user 2026-08-29 as the range to characterise: 2, 3, 4 mm. 🔴 NOT A CHOSEN VALUE — 3.0 is the middle of that range, recorded so the parameter has a home with provenance rather than living as a number on a command line. The sweep is what chooses it.
loop.azim.h.mm.verification: a run that quotes this must be a sweep OVER it, not a run that inherited it

loop.azim.arc.mm.description: AZIMUTHAL loop: ARC LENGTH along the wall. Unwound conductor = arc - port gap + 2h. 🔑 Length not angle: the angle depends on R = a - h, so specifying an angle would couple h and L, and they are meant to be independent axes.
loop.azim.arc.mm.source: STATED by the user 2026-08-29: lambda/10 = 12.24 mm plus brackets at 10.2 and 14.2. lambda/10 puts the loop well BELOW resonance, where it behaves as a lumped inductor — avoiding both the 39.6% conductor loss measured at lambda/4 and the tolerance sensitivity there (d ln Q_ext / d ln L = 4-6.5). 🔴 NOT CHOSEN; 12.24 is the centre of the declared range.

loop.strip.mm.description: Conductor cross-section [axial, radial] for a RECTANGULAR strip, or null for a round wire of loop.wire_r.mm. The AXIAL dimension is the wide one, so the broad face lies parallel to the wall.
loop.strip.mm.source: PROPOSED by the user 2026-08-29: compare a 1 mm round wire against a 5x1 mm strip, broad face to the wall, because the conductor's impedance shows up in the solve. null is the current default (round wire) — the strip is a case the sweep carries, not a choice yet.
loop.strip.mm.note: 🔴 A strip changes the loop-surface identification rule: it is 5 mm tall in z, not 2*loop.wire_r.mm, and geometry.py keys the loop attribute on exactly that. Handled — but any new cross-section must revisit it or the coupler silently reverts to the wall's aluminium.

provenance.hypothesis: first solve of the AZIMUTHAL topology — how does it differ?
provenance.question: How does the AZIMUTHAL loop differ from the rectangular one, and what does it do to VSWR? Grid: arc L in {10.2, 12.24, 14.2} mm x h in {2,3,4} mm, as a 1 mm wire and as a 5x1 mm strip laid flat against the wall. L and h are INDEPENDENT: unwound = L + 2h - gap, so the L+2h = 18.24 diagonal is an internal control on whether unwound length alone predicts Q_ext, or whether the split between azimuthal run and standoff matters.
provenance.prediction: Area ~20 mm^2 against the rectangular family's 140-180, and unwound conductor 18.2 mm = 0.60 lambda/4, well BELOW resonance. If coupling tracked area, Q_ext would be far higher than the family's 963-1,202 — possibly near 43,523, which is beta = 1 COLD and therefore an IGNITION coupler. ⚠️ Stated as a scale, not a prediction: the area model has been falsified twice this week.
provenance.verification: V1 the named probes must appear: arc_mid, wall_gap, leg_mid, port_gap, bore_edge, bore_mid. V2 the mesh sidecar must carry geometry_mm.loop_azim and the rig must bind clearance from it. V3 the loop must be COPPER on attribute 92 — the log says so per solve. V4 bore probes must reproduce closed-form TE011 to ~1%, as they do for the radial family.
provenance.falsification: 🔴 F1 if the probes do not emit, the comparison instrument does not exist for this topology and the grid is pointless. 🔴 F2 if Q_ext lands in the rectangular family's 963-1,202 band despite 8x less area, then area does not set coupling here either and the topology is not reaching a new regime. 🔴 F3 if purity or A2/A0 degrade markedly versus the radial loop's P >= 0.999, the arc perturbs TE011 more than the rectangle does, which would count against it regardless of Q_ext.
provenance.user: 'I need to see how azimuthal differs from rectangular'
provenance.note: Geometry verified before this run: wire and strip both mesh in 3-18 s at h = 2/3/4, one port face each, loop surface within 5-7% of analytic and the strip 1.95x the wire (perimeter ratio 1.91).
provenance.amended: 2026-08-30 — resume:false. The pec result was being REUSED from a checkpoint taken on the OLD annular-sector mesh, so the polyline mesh had never actually been solved and I could not tell a malformed mesh (MFEM STable3D abort) from a rejected port. Deleting result.json did not clear it; the flag does.
provenance.amended2: 2026-08-30 — port face radial half-width now DERIVED from Palace's lumped element tolerance. The annular sector's inner and outer arcs differ by 2*pw*rc*2psi; with 2psi = lg/R the relative mismatch is 2*pw*rc/R, measured at 1.048% for pw=0.9 against a 1% tolerance. Capped for a 2x margin. The mesh is otherwise unchanged and pec reproduces Q0 = 44,083.
provenance.amended3: 2026-08-30 — PORT FACE IS NOW FLAT, and this is what unblocked Q_ext. MEASURED, both rejected: an annular-sector port face mismatches Palace's bounding-box check by 2*pw*rc/R, independent of the gap — 1.048% at pw=0.9 and 0.249% at pw=0.2125, exactly proportional. The tolerance is therefore tighter than 0.25%, and reaching it would need a face ~42 um wide on a 2 mm conductor. No sector width works. A FLAT rectangle inset to the inner radius's offset (1.59 um short at the outer edge, 1.1% of the half-gap) meshes clean and Palace accepts it. ⚠️ UNVERIFIED at the time of launch: that the accepted face actually DRIVES. e0k2_anchor records a face inset by 2% floating and returning a flat S11 with no error raised. The first case is the reference geometry for exactly this reason — if its Q_ext is not finite and well below Q0, the face is floating and the whole grid is void.
provenance.amended4: 2026-08-30 — REDIRECTED mid-grid. h=4/L=12.24 TIMED OUT at 7200s after 556 NLEPS iterations (13 s/iter); h=4/L=14.2 is more strongly coupled still and was heading the same way, so the h=4 row costs ~4h for the two DEEPEST overcoupled points in the grid. Dropped. The saturation finding does not need them — it rests on h=4/L=10.2 (beta 4.486 vs area^4's 6.29). ADDED h=2 x L in {13.0, 13.4, 13.8} to MEASURE beta=1, which is currently only interpolated at L~13.4, and which is the number that decides VSWR. Strip cases kept but capped at h<=3 for the same timeout reason. 🔴 NOT a result: the h=4 row is DROPPED, not answered. h-saturation above 3 mm rests on ONE point.
provenance.amended5: 2026-08-30 — the three cold-critical wire cases (L = 13.0/13.4/13.8) are DROPPED, and the reason is the OBJECTIVE, not the difficulty. KNOWN's 2026-08-25 correction establishes that cold beta = 1 is the wrong target for a fixed loop: Q_ext serves two states whose Q0 differ ~265x, so a cold-critical loop is beta ~ 0.0024 loaded, VSWR ~ 416. The minimax is Q_ext = sqrt(Q0cold*Q0loaded) ~ 2,100, BELOW every Q_ext this grid measured (6,362-112,004). ⚠️ They were ALSO failing: L=13.0 lumped hit the 4000-iteration budget (worst converged run used 869) and L=13.4 PEC timed out at 7200s / 3599 iterations. pec has no port loading, so that is a MESH conditioning problem specific to the new arc lengths, NOT coupling. Unexplained and NOT chased, because the measurement is no longer wanted. If arcs outside {10.2, 12.24, 14.2} are ever needed, expect this and check the chord layout for slivers first. KEPT: the 6 strip cases, on arcs already known to mesh, for coupling STRENGTH only — eigen cannot report complex Z (see NEXT.md).
